stem: A trading company is building a browser dashboard that must push order status changes to the specific trader who placed each order within one second. Order events are produced by backend services into an SQS queue. Traders connect from browsers that cannot accept inbound connections, about 30,000 traders are online at peak, and the company wants a serverless design with no servers that hold connections. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Expose a REST API that browsers poll every second, with a Lambda function that reads pending updates for the caller from a DynamoDB table keyed by trader ID
Create one Amazon SNS topic per trader with an HTTPS subscription to each trader's browser, and publish each order update to the topic of its trader
Run an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions in front of a Lambda function that keeps WebSocket connections open and streams updates to each trader
Use an API Gateway WebSocket API that stores connection IDs by trader in DynamoDB on $connect, and a Lambda consumer that posts updates via the @connections API

stem: A live auction site uses an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API to push bid updates to browsers. Users report two problems: some lose updates after sitting on a quiet auction page for a while, and everyone watching long auctions is disconnected at exactly the same session age even while bids are flowing. Server logs show no errors and the service quotas for connections are not reached. Which TWO changes should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable API Gateway stage caching with a long TTL so that browsers reconnecting after a drop receive the bids they missed from the cache
Raise the API Gateway idle connection timeout setting on the WebSocket stage from 10 minutes to 8 hours in the stage settings for long auctions
Add client logic that detects a closed connection and reconnects automatically, since connections end at the 2-hour maximum duration regardless of traffic
Switch the WebSocket API to an edge-optimized endpoint type so CloudFront keeps connections alive past the API Gateway connection limits
Have the client send a small heartbeat message on a route at an interval shorter than the 10-minute idle timeout so quiet connections stay open

stem: An insurer has a core policy system on premises that exposes only a SOAP/XML web service reachable over AWS Direct Connect. New mobile and partner apps need a JSON REST API with request validation, per-partner API keys and throttling. The SOAP service cannot change and the company wants to avoid writing and running transformation code where configuration can do the job. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use CloudFront with a CloudFront Function that converts JSON request bodies into SOAP envelopes before forwarding them to the on-premises origin
Create an API Gateway HTTP API with parameter mapping to rewrite JSON bodies into SOAP envelopes, and use a VPC link to reach the on-premises service
Place an Application Load Balancer in front of the SOAP service with listener rules that rewrite JSON request bodies into XML and attach usage plans to the ALB
Create an API Gateway REST API with non-proxy HTTP integrations, mapping templates that convert JSON to SOAP XML and back, and a private integration via a VPC link

stem: A manufacturer runs dozens of legacy Java applications that exchange fixed-width text messages through a self-managed Apache ActiveMQ broker using JMS over OpenWire. The company wants to retire the broker hardware and let new cloud microservices react to these messages as JSON events routed by EventBridge rules. The legacy applications may change only their broker connection URL. Which solution meets these requirements with the least custom infrastructure?

choices.text: Migrate the broker to Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ and add a Lambda event source mapping on the queue that parses each message into JSON and calls PutEvents
Migrate to Amazon MSK and use a Kafka Connect connector to translate OpenWire traffic from the applications into Kafka records that feed EventBridge
Point the applications at an Amazon SNS topic with raw message delivery and use an EventBridge input transformer to parse the fixed-width text into JSON
Replace the broker with Amazon SQS FIFO queues and modify the legacy applications to use the AWS SDK so that EventBridge rules can read the queues directly

stem: A bank operates in a country where no AWS Region or Local Zone exists, and regulators require customer data to stay inside the bank's own data center. The bank wants to run new services with the same AWS APIs, tools and console it uses in the cloud, including EC2 instances, EBS volumes, a managed PostgreSQL database, and containers on Amazon EKS, while AWS handles hardware monitoring and replacement. The data center has a reliable connection to the nearest Region. Which solution fits?

choices.text: Register the bank's own servers with Amazon ECS Anywhere and Systems Manager, and run PostgreSQL and the services as ECS tasks on those servers
Install Amazon EKS Anywhere on the bank's VMware vSphere cluster and run PostgreSQL in containers managed by a Kubernetes operator on the same cluster
Order AWS Outposts racks for the data center, then run EC2, EBS, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL on Outposts, and EKS worker nodes on the Outposts subnets
Use AWS Local Zones attached to the nearest Region, placing EC2, EBS and RDS for PostgreSQL in the Local Zone subnet that is closest to the country

stem: A visual effects studio in Los Angeles runs its main workloads in us-west-2. Artists in the Los Angeles office use remote workstations and render nodes that need single-digit millisecond latency to their desks; from us-west-2 latency is around 20 ms. Demand spikes for a few weeks per project, and the studio has no data center space and does not want to commit to on-premises hardware. Which approach should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Keep the instances in us-west-2 and put AWS Global Accelerator in front of them so artist traffic uses the AWS backbone with lower latency
Order an AWS Outposts rack for the Los Angeles office and run the workstations and render nodes on it during project peaks before returning the rack
Opt in to the Los Angeles Local Zone, add a subnet there to the existing us-west-2 VPC, and run the workstations and render nodes in it
Deploy the workstations in an AWS Wavelength Zone in Los Angeles so artist traffic is carried by the carrier's 5G network to the instances

stem: A defense contractor must run containerized applications on bare-metal servers in a classified site that is air-gapped: no network path to any AWS Region is permitted. It wants Kubernetes with the same Amazon EKS Kubernetes distribution it uses in the cloud, lifecycle tooling for cluster creation and upgrades, and the option of a paid AWS support subscription. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes, joining the bare-metal servers as worker nodes to an EKS cluster whose control plane runs in the nearest AWS Region
Amazon ECS Anywhere, registering the bare-metal servers as external instances and running the applications as ECS tasks under a Regional cluster
AWS Outposts racks installed in the classified site, with EKS local clusters running both the Kubernetes control plane and the worker nodes
Amazon EKS Anywhere on the bare-metal servers, installed from a local registry with the air-gapped procedure, and an EKS Anywhere Enterprise Subscription

stem: A media company keeps 400 TB of viewing data in S3 as Hive-style partitioned Parquet tables. A privacy law now requires deleting a viewer's rows within 72 hours of a request, auditors want to query tables as they were on a past date, and engineers want to add columns without rewriting data. Data engineers use Spark on Amazon EMR, and analysts use Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift. Which approach meets these requirements with the least custom code?

choices.text: Convert the tables to Apache Iceberg tables registered in the Glue Data Catalog, use DELETE statements for requests and time travel queries for audits
Load all viewing data into Amazon Redshift tables, delete rows there, and use Redshift snapshots restored to new clusters for the auditors' historic queries
Keep the Parquet layout and run a nightly EMR job that rewrites every partition containing requested viewers, keeping a dated copy of each table for audits
Store each viewer's events as separate S3 objects under a viewer ID prefix and use S3 Lifecycle rules to expire the prefixes named in deletion requests

stem: A healthcare company's data lake has 900 tables in S3 cataloged in the Glue Data Catalog, and analysts query it with Amazon Athena. In the 40 claims tables, analysts in each region may see only rows for their own region; PII columns in any table must be hidden from everyone except a compliance group, and new tables arrive weekly. Today access is managed with IAM and S3 bucket policies per prefix, which cannot express these rules. Which solution meets the requirements with the least ongoing administration?

choices.text: Create Athena views per region that omit the PII columns, and use IAM policies so each regional analyst group can query only its own views
Write S3 bucket policies with s3:prefix and s3:ExistingObjectTag conditions that block reading the PII columns and the rows of other regions
Create one Athena workgroup per analyst region with a query result location and a per-query data scan limit, and allow each group to use only its own workgroup
Register the S3 locations with Lake Formation, grant access with LF-Tags on databases and columns, and use data filters for row-level restriction by region

stem: An e-commerce company already produces clickstream events to an Amazon MSK cluster used by several microservices. Business users want Amazon Redshift dashboards that reflect these events within about 10 seconds. The company wants to avoid staging the data in S3, avoid running additional ETL infrastructure, and keep SQL as the only transformation layer. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use AWS DMS with the MSK cluster as the source endpoint and Redshift as the target endpoint, running a full-load-and-CDC task that copies new records
Run an AWS Glue streaming job that reads the topic and writes micro-batches to S3, then load them with a Redshift COPY command every 10 seconds
Configure Redshift streaming ingestion with an external schema mapped to the MSK cluster and an auto-refreshing materialized view over the topic
Create an Amazon AppFlow flow with the MSK topic as the source and Redshift as the destination, configured to run on a schedule every minute

stem: A sales organization wants to combine Salesforce and ServiceNow data with 30 TB of order history in S3. A complex Apache Spark job joins the data once each night and runs for about 90 minutes; nothing else uses compute during the day. The team has no developers to maintain API integration code, wants to pay for Spark only while it runs, and does not want to tune or patch clusters. Which design is most cost-effective with the least operational effort?

choices.text: Use AWS DMS to replicate Salesforce and ServiceNow into S3, and submit the nightly Spark job to an EMR cluster that the team resizes before each run
Use scheduled Amazon AppFlow flows to land Salesforce and ServiceNow data in S3, and run the nightly Spark job on an Amazon EMR Serverless application
Write AWS Lambda functions that page through the Salesforce and ServiceNow APIs nightly, and run Spark on a persistent EMR cluster with On-Demand instances
Stream Salesforce and ServiceNow changes into Kinesis Data Streams with custom producers, and run Spark Structured Streaming on an EMR cluster all day

stem: A grocery retailer and a consumer goods brand want to measure how many of the brand's ad-exposed customers bought its products at the retailer. Each company keeps its customer data in S3 in its own AWS account. Legal teams require that neither party can see the other's row-level data, that only aggregated counts above a minimum group size can be returned, and that the retailer controls which queries are allowed on its table. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create an AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, configure each table with an aggregation analysis rule and minimum thresholds, and run the overlap query there
Replicate both datasets into a shared account with hashed email addresses and give both teams Athena access with a view that returns only aggregates
Share the retailer's table with the brand's account through AWS Lake Formation cross-account grants with a data filter that excludes the name and email columns
Publish the retailer's dataset as a private product on AWS Data Exchange for the brand, with subscription terms that forbid copying of row-level data

stem: A central data platform account owns a governed data lake: S3 data is registered with AWS Lake Formation and cataloged in the Glue Data Catalog. Twelve business-unit accounts in the same AWS Organization need to query selected databases with Amazon Athena in their own accounts, without copying data, while the platform team keeps central control of table and column permissions. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: In each business-unit account, run a Glue crawler against the platform account's S3 buckets to build a local copy of the tables in the account's catalog
Add a Glue Data Catalog resource policy that allows glue:* for the organization and a bucket policy granting s3:GetObject to all business-unit accounts
Replicate the governed S3 buckets to each business-unit account with S3 Replication and register the replicas with the business units' Lake Formation
In the platform account, grant Lake Formation permissions on the selected databases and tables (by name or LF-Tags) to each business-unit account
In each business-unit account, have the data lake administrator create resource links to the shared databases and grant local analyst roles access

stem: A company connects 35 VPCs in one Region through a transit gateway. Each VPC route table sends 10.0.0.0/8 to the transit gateway. A data lake VPC (10.20.0.0/16) and an analytics VPC (10.30.0.0/16) exchange about 400 TB per month, mostly between subnets in the same Availability Zones, which is now the largest line on the network bill. All other VPC pairs exchange little data and must keep using the transit gateway. Which change reduces cost the most with the least redesign?

choices.text: Enable appliance mode on both transit gateway VPC attachments so that the traffic between the two VPCs stays in the same Availability Zone and avoids the transit gateway processing charge
Move both VPCs into a separate transit gateway route table with only each other's routes so that their traffic is isolated and billed as attachment hours instead of per gigabyte
Create a VPC peering connection between the two VPCs and add routes for each other's /16 CIDR pointing to the peering connection, leaving the 10.0.0.0/8 route to the transit gateway in place
Publish the data lake as an endpoint service behind a Network Load Balancer and consume it from the analytics VPC through an interface endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink

stem: A company has 50 spoke VPCs in one Region connected through a transit gateway. Every spoke VPC has its own interface endpoints for 12 AWS services in three Availability Zones, and the endpoint hourly charges have become significant even though API traffic to those services is light. The same spokes also read several terabytes per day from Amazon S3 in the same Region. Which TWO changes lower the network cost while keeping traffic off the internet? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create the interface endpoints once in a shared services VPC, disable private DNS on them, and associate Route 53 private hosted zones for the service names with every spoke VPC
Create one S3 gateway endpoint in the shared services VPC and add a route in each spoke VPC that sends S3 prefix list traffic to that VPC through the transit gateway
Keep interface endpoints in every spoke but deploy them in a single Availability Zone, so each service needs one endpoint network interface per VPC instead of three
Delete the interface endpoints and send AWS API traffic through centralized NAT gateways in an egress VPC, which already serves internet-bound traffic from the spokes
Create an S3 gateway endpoint in each spoke VPC and add it to the spoke route tables, so S3 traffic goes directly to S3 without using the transit gateway

stem: A company replaced a full mesh of VPC peering connections between 12 VPCs with a single transit gateway to simplify routing. Traffic volumes and Availability Zone placement did not change, but the monthly networking bill rose sharply. Cost Explorer shows a large new line item for the transit gateway in the same Region. What is the most likely cause of the increase?

choices.text: The transit gateway charges inter-Region data transfer rates for traffic between attachments, because each attachment is treated as a separate network even within one Region
The transit gateway bills an hourly charge for every attachment and a per-GB data processing charge for traffic sent into it, neither of which applies to VPC peering
The transit gateway bills a charge for every propagated route in its route tables, and the 12 VPCs propagate many more routes than the peering connections did
The transit gateway enables appliance mode on every attachment by default, which sends each flow through an extra Availability Zone and doubles the data transfer charge

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with consolidated billing. Two months ago, platform teams began tagging all resources in member accounts with a CostCenter key, and the tags are visible on the resources in the console. The finance team, which works in the management account, still cannot group or filter by CostCenter in AWS Cost Explorer or see it as a column in the Cost and Usage Report. What should the company do?

choices.text: Attach a tag policy for CostCenter to the organization root with enforcement turned on, which publishes the tag key to the billing data of every member account
Create a Cost and Usage Report in each member account with resource IDs included, and join the reports with the tag values exported from the Resource Groups Tagging API
Activate CostCenter as a user-defined cost allocation tag on the cost allocation tags page of the management account and wait for the activation to take effect
Enable AWS Config in every member account and add the required-tags managed rule for CostCenter, so that billing can read the recorded tag values from the configuration items

stem: A company is designing cost allocation for 3 business units, about 40 projects and three environments (dev, test, prod). Finance wants every dollar assigned to a business unit and environment, including charges that cannot be tagged, such as some data transfer and support fees. Teams frequently create short-lived resources and sometimes forget tags. Which design meets these goals most reliably?

choices.text: Put all business units in one shared account per environment and depend on BusinessUnit, Project and Environment tags on every resource for each allocation dimension
Create accounts per project, use AWS-generated aws:createdBy tags to infer business unit and environment, and activate them as cost allocation tags for reporting
Use one large account for the whole company and assign costs to business units and environments each month by splitting the bill in proportion to vCPU hours
Create accounts per business unit and environment in OUs, so linked account data covers untagged charges, and require a Project tag on resources within each account

stem: A company tags EC2 instances with Project and Environment through an Auto Scaling group tag, and those cost allocation tags are activated. Cost Explorer correctly allocates instance costs, but the costs of the EBS volumes attached to those instances and of their daily snapshots appear under "No tag key". Snapshots are created by an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy. Which change fixes the allocation with the least ongoing effort?

choices.text: Activate the AWS-generated aws:createdBy cost allocation tag, which links each volume and snapshot to the Auto Scaling group that created the instance
Add volume tag specifications to the launch template, and enable the copy-tags option in the Data Lifecycle Manager policy so snapshots inherit the volume tags
Run a scheduled Lambda function every hour that copies tags from each instance to its volumes, and then from each volume to its newest snapshots
Create a cost category that assigns all EBS charges to projects in proportion to the EC2 instance hours each project used during the same billing month

stem: A company protects Amazon EFS file systems and Amazon DynamoDB tables with AWS Backup (advanced DynamoDB backup features are enabled). Requirements: daily backups kept 35 days for operational restores, and monthly backups kept 7 years for compliance; monthly backups are restored less than once a year. The company wants the lowest storage cost that still meets the retention rules. Which TWO backup plan settings should the solutions architect configure? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A daily rule that keeps recovery points for 35 days in warm storage with no transition to cold storage
A monthly rule that keeps recovery points in warm storage and a vault lifecycle rule that exports them to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
A daily rule that moves recovery points to cold storage after 7 days and deletes them after 35 days
A monthly rule that keeps recovery points for 90 days in a vault with AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode set to 7 years
A monthly rule that moves recovery points to cold storage after 30 days and keeps them for 7 years

stem: A company runs 400 EC2 instances with EBS volumes. Policy requires daily snapshots kept 14 days and quarterly snapshots kept 3 years for audits. Quarterly snapshots are almost never restored, and an audit restore that takes up to three days is acceptable. The company wants automation with no custom code and the lowest snapshot storage cost. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy with daily snapshots kept 14 days and a Recycle Bin retention rule that keeps deleted snapshots for 3 years as an audit copy
Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy with daily and quarterly schedules in the standard tier, and enable fast snapshot restore on the quarterly snapshots for audits
Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy with a daily schedule that archives every snapshot to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier one day after creation and retains it for 3 years
Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy with a daily schedule kept 14 days and a quarterly schedule that moves snapshots to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier for 3 years

stem: A company backs up EC2 instances, Amazon RDS databases and DynamoDB tables (advanced DynamoDB backup features are enabled) with AWS Backup in us-east-1. Daily backups are kept 30 days in the Region. For a Regional disaster, the business accepts losing up to 7 days of data and needs only the latest four weekly restore points in us-west-2. Cross-Region copy and storage costs must be minimized. What should the solutions architect do?

choices.text: Add a cross-Region copy action to the daily rule, keep the copies in us-west-2 for 7 days, and transition them to cold storage after 1 day to reduce the storage cost
Add a weekly rule with a copy action to a us-west-2 vault that keeps copies for 28 days, and leave the daily rule without any cross-Region copy action
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager cross-Region copy for all three resource types on a weekly schedule, with a retention of four copies in us-west-2
Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the backup vault in us-east-1 with a lifecycle rule in us-west-2 that deletes replicated recovery points after 28 days

stem: A company runs 30 stateless microservices on one Amazon EKS cluster in us-east-1, deployed by Argo CD from a Git repository, with images in Amazon ECR and data in an Aurora global database. A new requirement sets an RTO of 15 minutes for a Regional outage. Rebuilding a cluster and its add-ons during a test took over two hours. Which design meets the RTO with the least operational effort?

choices.text: Run a second EKS cluster in us-west-2 synced by Argo CD from the same repository, replicate images with ECR replication, and fail over DNS with Route 53 health checks
Use EKS Pod Identity associations in both Regions so the pods can authenticate in us-west-2, and redeploy the manifests there when the primary Region fails
Add a managed node group in us-west-2 subnets to the existing cluster, so pods can be scheduled in the second Region when us-east-1 nodes become unavailable
Take scheduled Velero backups of the cluster to S3 with Cross-Region Replication, and restore them into a new EKS cluster created in us-west-2 during a disaster

stem: A platform team runs all production workloads on a single large Amazon EKS cluster in one Region. Last quarter, a faulty cluster-wide add-on update and a misconfigured admission webhook each caused a full outage for every service. The team wants to limit the impact of cluster-level failures and upgrade clusters without risking all traffic at once, while staying in one Region for data residency. Which approach best meets these goals?

choices.text: Split workloads across separate managed node groups for each team inside the existing cluster, and apply add-on updates to one node group at a time
Enable EKS control plane logging and CloudWatch alarms on API server errors so that operators can roll back a faulty add-on more quickly
Run two or more identical clusters in the Region behind Route 53 weighted records, and shift traffic away from one cluster before changing it
Enroll the cluster in EKS extended support so that Kubernetes version upgrades can be postponed until the team has more time for testing

stem: A company runs a customer-facing API on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate in eu-west-1, behind an Application Load Balancer, with data in DynamoDB global tables that already replicate to eu-central-1. The company needs an active-active deployment across both Regions, failover within one minute without relying on DNS TTLs, and no dependency on eu-west-1 when it fails. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Run an ECS cluster, service and ALB in each Region, replicate images with ECR replication, and add both ALBs as endpoint groups of an AWS Global Accelerator
Run an ECS service in each Region that pulls images from the eu-west-1 ECR repository, and put both ALBs behind one CloudFront distribution with an origin group
Create one ECS cluster with a capacity provider in each Region, pull images from the eu-west-1 ECR repository, and use Route 53 latency records for the two load balancers
Run the ECS service only in eu-west-1 with the deployment circuit breaker enabled, so failed tasks are automatically relaunched in eu-central-1 during an outage

stem: A company plans its first AWS Fault Injection Service experiment in production: a network disruption on the EC2 instances of a checkout service that runs across three Availability Zones. Leadership requires that the experiment affects only a small share of capacity at first and stops automatically if customers are affected. Which experiment template configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Target instances by tag with a selection mode of ALL, and assign an on-call engineer to watch dashboards and stop the experiment manually if errors appear
Target instances by tag with a selection mode of COUNT(1), and set a stop condition on a CloudWatch alarm for CPU utilization of the targeted instances
Target instances by tag with a selection mode of PERCENT(10), and set a stop condition on a CloudWatch alarm for checkout error rate and p99 latency
Target instances by tag with a selection mode of PERCENT(10), and add an EventBridge rule that deletes the experiment template when an error alarm fires

stem: A team ran the AWS Fault Injection Service "AZ Availability: Power Interruption" scenario against a staging copy of an order platform. After the run, engineers disagreed whether it passed: some pointed to instance replacements, others to a short error spike, and nobody knew how much impact was acceptable. Which TWO changes make the next experiment produce a clear pass or fail result? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Expand the experiment to impair all three Availability Zones at once so that any weakness produces a larger, unmistakable error spike that every engineer can recognize
Express the hypothesis limits as CloudWatch alarms, use them as the experiment's stop conditions, and compare the metrics during the run with the baseline period before it
Use the AWS Config compliance status of the affected resources at the end of the experiment as the pass or fail signal, because Config records every configuration change
Measure success by whether all EC2 instances in the impaired Availability Zone are replaced within the scenario duration, because replacement proves that self-healing works
Before the run, write a steady-state hypothesis with measurable customer metrics and limits, such as order success rate above 99.5 percent and p99 latency under 400 ms during the disruption

stem: A payments application spans three AWS accounts: one for the API tier on Amazon EKS, one for Amazon RDS databases and one for shared networking. A central resilience team in a fourth account wants to run one AWS Fault Injection Service experiment that disrupts resources in all three accounts at the same time, with one set of stop conditions and one experiment record. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Share the target resources from the three accounts with the resilience account through AWS RAM, so a single-account experiment template there can select them as targets
Create an experiment template in each of the three accounts and start them together from an AWS Step Functions state machine in the resilience account at the same timestamp
Deploy the same experiment template to all three accounts with CloudFormation StackSets and give each account its own stop condition alarm on its local metrics
Create a multi-account experiment template in the resilience account with target account configurations, using roles in each target account that trust the resilience account's FIS role

stem: A company runs six Amazon EKS clusters on EC2 nodes across two Regions. Operations needs cluster, node, pod and container level CPU, memory and network metrics, curated dashboards, and container logs in CloudWatch, with the least effort to install and keep updated on every cluster. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Install the Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on on each cluster to enable Container Insights with enhanced observability and Fluent Bit log collection
Install the CloudWatch agent on every worker node with Systems Manager State Manager, and publish instance CPU, memory and disk metrics with detailed monitoring
Enable EKS control plane logging for the api, audit and scheduler log types on all six clusters, and build CloudWatch dashboards from the resulting log groups
Deploy a self-managed Prometheus server and Grafana in each cluster with Helm charts, and forward container logs to CloudWatch with a Fluentd daemonset per cluster

stem: An Amazon ECS service on AWS Fargate runs tasks with three containers each. Tasks are restarting several times a day, and the service's CloudWatch metrics show memory utilization of only 60 percent. The team suspects one container is reaching its memory limit but cannot see per-task or per-container metrics. Which action gives the needed visibility with the least effort?

choices.text: Use ECS Exec to open a shell in each running container and run the top command periodically to record memory usage before each restart occurs
Enable AWS X-Ray tracing in the application code so that traces record container memory usage for each request that the service handles
Enable CloudWatch Container Insights with enhanced observability for the cluster, and review task and container memory metrics on its dashboards
Turn on EC2 detailed monitoring for the cluster so that one-minute memory metrics are published for each task and each container in the service

stem: An online retailer's checkout has failed twice at night after a third-party payment script changed, and nobody noticed until morning because traffic was very low. Separately, the business wants to know how page load times and JavaScript errors differ by browser and country for real shoppers. Which TWO solutions should the solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable ALB access logs and query them with Amazon Athena to measure page load time and errors per browser and per country for all customer sessions
Create a CloudWatch RUM app monitor and add its JavaScript snippet to the web pages to collect page load timings, JavaScript errors and session data
Instrument the backend services with AWS X-Ray and group the traces by the user agent and source country that the load balancer records for each request
Create Amazon Route 53 health checks against the checkout URL with string matching enabled, and alarm when the health check status changes to unhealthy
Create a CloudWatch Synthetics canary that scripts the browse, add-to-cart and test checkout flow every five minutes, with an alarm on the canary success metric

stem: A company created a CloudWatch Synthetics API canary to test an internal service behind an internal Application Load Balancer. The canary is configured to run in the VPC's private subnets with a security group that allows outbound HTTPS. The private subnets have no NAT gateway and only an S3 gateway endpoint. The canary log shows the requests to the service succeeding, but the canary's SuccessPercent and Duration metrics never appear in CloudWatch, so the alarm on them stays in INSUFFICIENT_DATA. What is the most likely fix?

choices.text: Move the canary out of the VPC and attach a public IP address to the internal load balancer so the canary can reach it while still publishing metrics normally
Increase the canary's timeout and memory settings, because canaries inside a VPC need extra time to create network interfaces before every run
Change the canary runtime version to the newest one, because older runtimes cannot resolve internal load balancer names when they run inside a VPC
Add a CloudWatch monitoring interface endpoint (or a NAT gateway) to the private subnets so the canary can publish its metrics to CloudWatch

stem: A media company added CloudWatch RUM to a website that serves about 60 million sessions a month. The first bill was far above budget. Product managers need trend data on page load performance and error rates, not every session, and privacy rules forbid collecting more user data than needed. Which change best reduces cost while keeping useful real-user insight?

choices.text: Keep every session but disable the X-Ray integration of the app monitor, because RUM bills each event according to its number of trace segments
Lower the app monitor's session sample rate to a small percentage and collect only the telemetry types needed, such as performance and errors
Shorten the retention of the RUM app monitor's data in CloudWatch Logs to one day so that the stored telemetry is deleted before it can be billed
Replace RUM with a Synthetics canary that loads the home page every minute, because canaries represent the average experience of all real users

stem: A retail bank is launching three generative AI assistants on Amazon Bedrock. Each assistant uses a different foundation model. Compliance requires that no assistant gives personalized investment recommendations, that account numbers never appear in a response although the assistant must still answer the rest of the question, and that jailbreak attempts in user prompts are stopped. The security team wants one centrally owned control that all three assistants reuse and that does not depend on how each model follows instructions. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create one guardrail with a word filter that lists investment terms such as stock and fund, and a sensitive-information filter that blocks any response containing an account number pattern

Add a shared system prompt that forbids investment advice and account numbers, and enable model invocation logging so that a compliance analyst can review samples of each assistant's conversations every day

Fine-tune each of the three foundation models on curated conversations that refuse investment questions and omit account numbers, and run Amazon Comprehend PII detection on every response before display
Create one guardrail with a denied topic for investment advice, a regex sensitive-information filter that masks account numbers, and a prompt attack filter, and pass its version on every call

stem: An insurance company runs a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant on Amazon Bedrock that answers questions about policy documents retrieved from a knowledge base. A guardrail with content filters set to High is attached. Auditors found answers that cite coverage limits that appear nowhere in the retrieved passages, and answers that drift to unrelated subjects when users ask narrow questions. The company wants such responses blocked automatically before users see them. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Raise the misconduct and violence content filters on model outputs from High to the maximum setting, and attach a second guardrail version to the knowledge base retrieval call
Set the model temperature to 0 and top-p to a low value for every request, and add a word filter that lists the coverage limit values that the policy documents contain
Enable the contextual grounding check with grounding and relevance thresholds, and pass the retrieved passages as the grounding source and the user question as the query

Add a denied topic to the guardrail named fabricated coverage information with sample phrases of invented limits, and raise the prompt attack filter to High so that misleading prompts are rejected at input

stem: A company runs two assistants on Amazon Bedrock: an internal HR assistant that may discuss salary bands with employees, and a public careers chatbot that must never discuss compensation. Both must mask email addresses and phone numbers in responses. Compliance requires that every guardrail policy change is tested before it reaches production, that production behavior never changes without an approved release, and that auditors can tell exactly which policy configuration each application used on a given date. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Change and test the guardrail's working draft in a staging environment, then publish a numbered guardrail version and point production at that version only after the release is approved
Keep the compensation and PII rules as versioned system prompt text in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and log which parameter version each assistant loaded at startup
Create one shared guardrail that contains the compensation denied topic, and have the HR assistant switch that topic off on each request by passing a policy override in the guardrail configuration
Point both production assistants at the guardrail's working draft so that an approved edit takes effect at once in every application, without any separate code or configuration release
Create a separate guardrail for each assistant from one shared infrastructure-as-code template, with the common PII masking in both and the compensation denied topic only in the chatbot guardrail

stem: A media company uses Amazon Bedrock with a guardrail for its chat products. It also runs a fine-tuned open-weight model on an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint and calls a third-party model provider's API for translation. The trust and safety team requires that prompts and responses for all three paths pass through exactly the same content, denied-topic and PII policies, maintained in one place, with no change of model providers. Which approach meets these requirements with the least operational effort?

choices.text: Import the fine-tuned model with Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import, move the translation workload to a Bedrock model, and attach the existing guardrail to every model invocation
Call the ApplyGuardrail API with the existing guardrail on each prompt before it is sent to the SageMaker endpoint or third-party API, and again on each response before returning it
Add a guardrail configuration to the SageMaker endpoint configuration, and ask the third-party provider to call the company's guardrail from its side through a cross-account IAM role
Put Amazon API Gateway in front of the SageMaker endpoint and the third-party API, and attach AWS WAF with AWS managed rule groups and custom string-match rules for blocked topics

stem: A healthcare provider uses Amazon Bedrock to summarize clinician notes for a care-coordination portal. Patient names and phone numbers must never appear in the summaries, but every note must still produce a usable summary. The compliance team also needs ongoing evidence of how often the guardrail acts on outputs. The current guardrail uses a sensitive-information filter with the Block action for names and phone numbers, and many summaries are being replaced by the blocked message. What change best meets the requirements?

choices.text: Remove the guardrail and instruct the model in the prompt to replace names and phone numbers with placeholders, then sample summaries manually each week for compliance evidence
Replace the sensitive-information filter with a denied topic named patient identity, and log every blocked response to CloudWatch Logs for the compliance team to review each week
Change the name and phone entity actions to mask (anonymize) so matches become placeholders, and use the guardrail trace and its CloudWatch metrics on interventions as evidence
Keep the Block action and add an Amazon Macie job that scans the portal's S3 export bucket each day, with findings sent to Security Hub CSPM as compliance evidence of guardrail activity

stem: A company runs a nightly reconciliation agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. No user is signed in while it runs. The agent calls a payment partner's API, which accepts only OAuth 2.0 access tokens that the partner's authorization server issues through the client credentials grant with narrow scopes. Security requires that the client secret never appears in agent code, container images or environment variables, that the agent receives short-lived tokens only for its own workload identity, and that future agents can reuse the same managed pattern. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Configure an AgentCore Identity OAuth credential provider for the partner with the authorization code flow, have an operations engineer consent once, and let the token vault refresh that engineer's token every night
Have the build pipeline read the client secret from AWS Secrets Manager and write it into the container image as a KMS-encrypted file that the agent decrypts with its execution role at startup
Grant the runtime execution role permission to a private API Gateway API that forwards each request to the partner, and sign every agent call with SigV4 by using the runtime's temporary credentials
Configure an AgentCore Identity OAuth credential provider for the partner with the client credentials (machine-to-machine) flow, and have the agent request scoped access tokens at run time

stem: A company hosts five AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime in a central AI platform account. The agents call tools implemented as AWS Lambda functions that are owned by business-unit accounts in the same organization. Each business unit must decide which agents may invoke its functions, each agent may call only the functions approved for it, a compromised agent must not be able to call another agent's tools, and no long-term credentials may be used. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Give each agent runtime its own execution role that allows lambda:InvokeFunction only on its approved function ARNs, and add a resource-based policy to each function that allows only the approved agents' role ARNs
Use one shared execution role for all five agents that allows lambda:InvokeFunction on every function in the organization, and list in each agent's system prompt the tools that it is allowed to call

Create an IAM user with invoke rights in each business-unit account, store its access keys in AWS Secrets Manager in the platform account, and let each agent read the keys of the business units it uses

Have each business unit add a resource-based policy to its functions that names the central platform account as the principal, and grant every agent execution role lambda:InvokeFunction on all resources

stem: An ecommerce company is building a customer support agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The agent has two tools: one returns order status and one issues refunds. A threat model highlights that a prompt injection in a customer message or a product review could make the agent refund another customer's order or exceed the 200 USD refund limit. Which combination of controls most effectively limits the impact of such an attack? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Give the agent a single execution role with full read and write access to the orders and payments tables so that both tools can run efficiently from one shared code path
Expose each tool as a separate AgentCore Gateway target backed by its own Lambda function, each with an execution role limited to the tables and actions that one tool needs
Add a denied topic for refunds to the guardrail used by the agent so that any message about refunds is blocked at input before the agent can consider calling the refund tool
Add instructions to the agent's system prompt stating that refunds above 200 USD are forbidden and that the agent must refuse requests concerning orders of other customers
Enforce the refund limit and order ownership inside the refund tool's backend, checking each order against the authenticated customer of the session rather than fields the model supplies

stem: A SaaS company runs one AI agent for several hundred tenants. The agent's tools read and write tenant data in a shared Amazon DynamoDB table whose partition key starts with the tenant ID. Tenants authenticate with Amazon Cognito, and the tenant ID is a claim in the access token. The company must guarantee that a tool call made for one tenant can never read another tenant's items, even if the model is manipulated into supplying another tenant's ID, and it wants to avoid per-tenant infrastructure. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Have the tool code filter the query results by comparing each item's tenant attribute with the tenant ID argument the model supplies to the tool, and log any mismatches for review
Add the tenant ID to the agent's system prompt for each session and instruct the model to always pass that ID to the tools, then enable a guardrail denied topic for other tenants' data
Deploy a separate agent runtime, tool set and DynamoDB table for each tenant in its own AWS account through an account vending pipeline, and route requests to the right account by subdomain
Have tools assume a role with a session tag set from the validated token's tenant claim, under a policy using dynamodb:LeadingKeys matched to the aws:PrincipalTag tenant value

stem: A company with 200 accounts in AWS Organizations allows Amazon Bedrock for experimentation. After a legal review, only four foundation models are approved for use. Platform teams must be able to keep using Bedrock management APIs such as guardrail and knowledge base operations. Security wants a preventive control that member account administrators cannot override and that requires no per-account work when new accounts are created. What should a solutions architect implement?

choices.text: A permissions boundary in every account that allows only the approved model ARNs, with an AWS Lambda function that attaches the boundary to every new role created in member accounts
An AWS Config organization rule that detects invocations of unapproved models in AWS CloudTrail data and invokes an SSM Automation runbook to detach the calling role's Bedrock permissions
An SCP on the root that denies Bedrock inference actions unless the resource is one of the approved foundation model or inference profile ARNs, leaving other Bedrock actions alone
A guardrail in every account with denied topics that describe the unapproved models' names, so that prompts which mention those models are blocked before inference starts

stem: A company uses a generative AI agent to analyze AWS Config and Security Hub CSPM findings and propose remediation plans, such as changing security group rules or stopping instances. Policy requires that a named on-call engineer approves every plan before any change is made, that approvals can take up to 3 days, that rejected plans are recorded, and that the whole flow is auditable. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Run an AWS Step Functions Standard workflow with a waitForTaskToken task that sends the plan and token to the engineer, then resumes on SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure
Run an AWS Step Functions Express workflow that sends the plan to the engineer by email and uses a Wait state of 3 days before a Choice state checks a DynamoDB item for the decision
Have a Lambda function send the plan to the engineer and poll a DynamoDB table every minute until the engineer records a decision, then apply or discard the plan from the same invocation
Write each plan to an Amazon SQS queue with a 3-day delivery delay so that engineers have time to review it in the console, and have a Lambda function apply the plan when the message becomes visible

stem: A Step Functions Standard workflow pauses on a waitForTaskToken task until a reviewer approves an AI-generated contract summary. The task has TimeoutSeconds set to 86400. Reviewers report that approval links clicked on Monday morning for requests sent on Friday return an error, and the summaries are never published. The approval API's logs show that SendTaskSuccess fails with TaskTimedOut for those tokens. The business wants requests to stay open over weekends and stale requests to be escalated rather than silently dropped. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Add HeartbeatSeconds of 86400 to the task and call SendTaskHeartbeat from the approval API each time a reviewer opens the link, so that the token is refreshed before it is used
Raise TimeoutSeconds to cover the longest expected wait, and add a Catch for States.Timeout that routes to an escalation state which notifies a manager and re-sends the request
Convert the workflow to an Express workflow so that executions are retained longer, and store the task tokens in DynamoDB with a time to live of one week to keep them valid
Generate a new task token in the approval API when the original token has expired, and call SendTaskSuccess with the new token so that the paused execution can continue from the same state

stem: A pharmaceutical company generates marketing copy with Amazon Bedrock. Every draft passes automated checks: a guardrail and a claims-validation Lambda function. Regulations require that any draft flagged by either check is reviewed by an authorized medical-legal reviewer before publication, that unflagged drafts publish without delay, and that each decision records which reviewer made it. Reviewers are employees who sign in through the corporate identity provider. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Publish all drafts immediately and have reviewers read flagged drafts later from a CloudWatch Logs Insights query, unpublishing any draft that they reject within one business day
Send every draft, flagged or not, to an Amazon Augmented AI human loop that uses the Amazon Mechanical Turk public workforce so that reviews finish quickly at any time of day
In a Step Functions Standard workflow, use a Choice state that publishes unflagged drafts directly and sends flagged drafts to a waitForTaskToken task that notifies reviewers
Store flagged drafts in an S3 bucket and let any employee with console access approve a draft by adding an approved object tag, which triggers publication through an S3 event notification
Build the review app behind Amazon Cognito federated with the corporate IdP, verify reviewer group membership in the backend, and call SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure with the reviewer ID

stem: A logistics company is giving an AI operations agent the ability to act on its AWS environment. Most actions, such as restarting a failed task or scaling a service within preset limits, must complete within seconds without people. Actions that delete resources, change IAM, or affect production databases must never run without human approval. Leadership is concerned about both approval fatigue and the agent talking itself out of asking for approval. Which design best balances these concerns?

choices.text: Route proposed actions through a Step Functions workflow whose Choice state applies a fixed rule set (action type, target, limits); only high-risk actions wait on a callback approval task
Instruct the agent in its system prompt to classify each action's risk level itself and to request approval through a chat tool whenever it judges that an action could be destructive
Let the agent run every action immediately with broad permissions, record all actions in CloudTrail, and have engineers review the trail daily and roll back any harmful change afterward
Require human approval for every action through a Step Functions callback task, so that no action can run without review and the risk of misclassification is eliminated completely

stem: A bank fine-tunes credit-risk models in Amazon SageMaker AI. Model risk management requires that no model version reaches the production endpoint until a member of the independent validation team approves it, that data scientists cannot approve their own models, that the approval status is stored with the exact model version, and that deployment starts automatically after approval. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Have data scientists open a ticket for each model version and attach validation evidence, then let them run the deployment pipeline themselves once the ticket is marked as resolved
Store each model artifact in Amazon S3 and let validators add an approved object tag, with an S3 event notification that triggers deployment of any object that carries the approved tag
Use SageMaker Model Monitor on the production endpoint to compare each new version against a baseline, and roll back automatically if data quality drifts beyond a threshold after deployment
Register versions in SageMaker Model Registry as PendingManualApproval, allow only the validator role to update approval status, and deploy from an EventBridge rule on the Approved status change

stem: A government contractor stores engineering data in Amazon S3 encrypted with AWS KMS symmetric keys and sends the same data between on-premises sites and AWS over TLS connections that use classical elliptic-curve key exchange. The data must stay confidential for at least 25 years. A security review warns that an adversary may be recording traffic today. The company has a limited budget for its first post-quantum project. Which action addresses the most urgent risk?

choices.text: Re-encrypt all S3 objects with new KMS keys and shorten key rotation to 90 days, because the symmetric keys that protect data at rest are the first targets of a quantum computer
Replace all code-signing and document-signing keys with ML-DSA keys first, because forged signatures are the main risk of traffic that adversaries record today
Move connections carrying this data to TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange (classical ECDHE combined with ML-KEM) on clients and endpoints that support it
Increase every RSA and ECDSA key used for TLS certificates to the largest available size, because larger classical keys keep recorded sessions secure against quantum attacks

stem: A medical device manufacturer ships infusion pumps that stay in service for 15 years and accept only firmware with a valid signature. The current signing key is an ECDSA key in AWS KMS. The company wants new devices to verify firmware with a post-quantum signature, the private key must never leave FIPS-validated hardware, and devices verify offline. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create a KMS key with an ML-KEM key spec, use it to sign each firmware image, and embed the corresponding public key in the device bootloader so that devices can verify updates offline
Create a KMS asymmetric key with an ML-DSA key spec and SIGN_VERIFY usage, sign each release with the KMS Sign API, and embed the public key from GetPublicKey in device firmware
Create a KMS HMAC key, generate a MAC over each firmware image with GenerateMac, and provision the HMAC key into each device's secure element so that the device can verify the image offline
Replace the ECDSA P-256 key with an ECDSA P-521 key in KMS, because the longer curve gives enough security margin against quantum attacks for the 15-year device lifetime

stem: A financial services company with about 400 applications wants to prepare for post-quantum cryptography. Applications use AWS KMS keys, certificates from AWS Certificate Manager and AWS Private CA, TLS libraries embedded in code, and several hard-coded algorithm choices. The CISO wants to be able to replace algorithms quickly as standards and AWS support evolve, without rewriting every application each time. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend first? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Build a cryptographic inventory of where asymmetric algorithms are used, including KMS key specs, certificate key algorithms, TLS settings and libraries, ranked by data lifetime
Replace AES-256 with a larger symmetric cipher across all storage services, because symmetric encryption is the most exposed component once quantum computers become practical
Wait to start any work until NIST publishes its first standards for post-quantum key encapsulation and digital signatures, because no standardized algorithms are available yet today
Immediately disable all classical key exchange and signature algorithms on every endpoint, so that only post-quantum algorithms are accepted from the first day of the program
Move algorithm choices out of application code into shared libraries and configuration, referencing KMS keys by alias so key types can change without code changes or redeployment

stem: Security architects are deciding how to configure TLS between an internal client fleet and AWS service endpoints for traffic that must resist future quantum attacks. One proposal uses only ML-KEM for key establishment. Another proposal uses a hybrid key exchange that combines X25519 with ML-KEM-768 in TLS 1.3. Why do AWS and most standards bodies recommend the hybrid approach for this transition?

choices.text: The hybrid mode encrypts each record twice, once with an AES key from X25519 and once with an AES key from ML-KEM, so that a break of either cipher still leaves the data protected
ML-KEM alone works only with TLS 1.2, so the hybrid approach is required to use TLS 1.3 and its faster handshake together with post-quantum protection on AWS endpoints
The hybrid key exchange produces smaller handshake messages than either algorithm alone, which lowers latency enough to offset the cost of the additional post-quantum computation
The session key is derived from both shared secrets, so it stays secure unless both algorithms are broken, which hedges against undiscovered flaws in the newer ML-KEM

stem: An on-premises application retrieves database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager over the internet. To counter harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks, the security team asked for post-quantum protection on these connections. The team rotated the secret, re-encrypted it with a new KMS key, and moved traffic onto AWS Site-to-Site VPN. A packet capture still shows TLS 1.3 handshakes with a classical X25519 key share only. What is the most likely cause, and what should the team do?

choices.text: The application's TLS client did not offer a hybrid ML-KEM key share; configure the AWS SDK with an HTTP client and TLS library that supports hybrid post-quantum key exchange
Secrets Manager negotiates post-quantum TLS only when the secret is encrypted with a KMS key that has an ML-DSA key spec, so re-encrypt the secret with an ML-DSA key and repeat the test
Post-quantum key exchange must be turned on for each secret with a resource policy condition, so add a statement that denies GetSecretValue when the request is not quantum-safe
Post-quantum TLS is available only through VPC interface endpoints, so create a Secrets Manager interface endpoint and route the application's traffic through it from on premises

stem: A company fine-tuned a model in Amazon Bedrock in its central AI account and runs it on Provisioned Throughput purchased in that account. Applications in 25 workload accounts, all in one OU of AWS Organizations, must invoke this model. Security requires least privilege and no long-lived credentials, and accounts that join the OU later must get access without changes in the AI account. Which solution meets these requirements most cost-effectively?

choices.text: In each workload account, attach an identity policy to the application role that allows bedrock:InvokeModel on the AI account's provisioned model ARN, and call that ARN directly from the application
Create a role in the AI account that trusts the OU through an aws:PrincipalOrgPaths condition, allow only bedrock:InvokeModel on the provisioned model ARN, and have applications assume it
Create Amazon Bedrock long-term API keys for an IAM user in the AI account, store one key in AWS Secrets Manager in each workload account, and rotate all of the keys manually every 90 days
Share the custom model with every workload account, buy Provisioned Throughput for it in each of those accounts, and let each application invoke the provisioned copy in its own account

stem: An insurer receives 40,000 claim submissions per day in Amazon S3: PDF claim forms in many layouts from different brokers, photos of damage and recorded phone statements. A downstream claims system needs the policy number, incident date and claimed amount from each form as JSON in a fixed schema, plus a text description of each photo and a transcript summary of each statement. The company wants a managed generative AI service and little custom code when a broker adds a new form layout. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Index all submissions in an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base, then have a Lambda function query the knowledge base for each field of every new submission and assemble the JSON record
Use Amazon Textract for forms, Amazon Rekognition for photos and Amazon Transcribe for audio, and write a Lambda parser for each form layout that maps the output into the schema
Fine-tune an Amazon Bedrock model on labelled claim forms whenever a broker adds a new layout, then invoke it from Lambda with each file's raw bytes to produce the JSON fields
Create an Amazon Bedrock Data Automation project whose blueprints define the claim fields, invoke it asynchronously for each new S3 object, and store the JSON output it writes to S3

stem: A company's document assistant calls an Anthropic Claude model in Amazon Bedrock through InvokeModel with Anthropic-specific request bodies, including tool definitions. Leadership has approved an Amazon Nova model as an automatic fallback when the primary model is throttled, wants either model swapped by configuration without redeploying code, and wants a single code path for both providers. Which actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router that contains the Claude and Nova models, and invoke the router ARN so that throttled requests move to Nova
Create one application inference profile that lists both the Claude and Nova models, and invoke its ARN so that Bedrock fails over from one model to the other
Move the calls to the Converse API so that messages, inference parameters and tool definitions share one request and response format for both providers' models
Keep InvokeModel and add a Lambda function for each provider that converts the Anthropic request body into the other provider's format before each fallback call
Keep the model IDs in AWS AppConfig, read them at run time, and when a call fails with a throttling exception, retry the same request with the fallback model ID

stem: A bank has 40 application accounts that want to use foundation models. The platform team must enforce a per-team monthly request budget and rate limit, log every prompt and response centrally in one account, allow only approved models, and be able to switch an approved model to another provider later without application teams changing code. Traffic must stay off the public internet. Which architecture meets these requirements?

choices.text: Let each account call Bedrock directly through its own interface endpoint, use an SCP to allow only approved model IDs, and enable invocation logging in every account to a central bucket
Build a gateway in a shared account: private API Gateway API with per-team usage plans, a Lambda function that calls the approved model via the Converse API, and central logging
Deploy an AWS Marketplace model on a SageMaker AI endpoint in a shared account, share the endpoint with AWS RAM, and use endpoint auto scaling limits as team budgets
Create a role in a central account that every team assumes to call Bedrock directly, and set Bedrock service quotas in that account to the sum of the team budgets

stem: A bank's on-premises applications must call Amazon Bedrock in eu-west-1 over its existing AWS Direct Connect connection, which reaches a shared services VPC through a transit gateway. Bedrock traffic must not traverse the internet, the applications must keep using the standard regional Bedrock runtime endpoint name in their SDKs, and any Bedrock invocation by the bank's application roles that does not come through the bank's own network path must be denied. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Add a public virtual interface to the Direct Connect connection, advertise the Bedrock public prefixes to on-premises routers, and deny invocation unless aws:SourceIp is in the bank's public address range
Create a bedrock-runtime interface endpoint in the shared VPC, keep public DNS resolution on premises, and add an endpoint policy that allows invocation only for the bank's application roles

Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon Bedrock in the shared services VPC, add the transit gateway attachment routes to its prefix list, and deny invocation unless the aws:SourceVpc condition key matches the VPC

Create a bedrock-runtime interface endpoint with private DNS in the shared VPC, forward Bedrock names from on-premises DNS to a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint, and deny calls without that aws:SourceVpce

stem: A logistics company built a planning agent with the open-source LangGraph framework. Each user conversation can run multi-step tool calls for up to 3 hours, sessions must be strictly isolated from each other because they hold customer data in memory, and the team wants no servers or clusters to manage. The agent must keep using LangGraph and a model hosted outside Amazon Bedrock for some steps. Which hosting option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Deploy the agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, which runs each session in its own isolated microVM, supports long-running sessions, and accepts any framework and model
Run the agent on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions so that each conversation stays on the task that started it
Package the agent as an AWS Lambda container image behind API Gateway and store intermediate state in DynamoDB between invocations of each multi-step plan
Recreate the agent as an Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic agent with action groups that call the external model, and attach session attributes for each user conversation

stem: A retailer is building several AI agents that must call existing internal capabilities: 30 REST APIs that already have OpenAPI specifications and 12 AWS Lambda functions. The agents use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to discover tools. The company wants one managed entry point that authenticates agents with OAuth, lets agents find the right tool among many, and avoids writing and hosting a separate MCP server for each API. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Place all APIs and Lambda functions behind one Amazon API Gateway REST API with a Cognito authorizer, and give each agent the exported OpenAPI file of that API as a prompt
Write one MCP server per API and per Lambda function, run them as Amazon ECS services behind an internal Application Load Balancer, and register each with the agents
Create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with the OpenAPI specs and Lambda functions as targets, inbound OAuth authorization, and semantic search over tools enabled
Load the OpenAPI specifications and Lambda function descriptions into an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base, and let agents retrieve the matching description before calling them

stem: A professional services firm is building an AgentCore-hosted assistant that books meetings in each consultant's own Google Calendar and reads their files in a third-party SaaS drive. Every action must run with the individual user's consent and permissions, never with a shared admin account. Security forbids the agent code from storing or handling refresh tokens, and users must not be asked to sign in again for every request. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with OAuth credential providers for the SaaS services so user-consented tokens are kept in its token vault and given to the agent per call
Store one SaaS administrator API key in AWS Secrets Manager, rotate it every 30 days with a Lambda rotation function, and filter results in the agent code by user email
Have the agent run the OAuth flow itself, encrypt each user's refresh token with AWS KMS, store it in DynamoDB keyed by user ID, and refresh access tokens in the agent code
Use an Amazon Cognito identity pool to exchange each user's token for temporary AWS credentials and have the agent call the SaaS APIs by signing requests with those credentials

stem: An airline is building a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. The agent must answer questions from 40,000 policy and fare-rule documents stored in Amazon S3, and it must remember each traveller's stated preferences (seat, meal, loyalty tier questions) across separate conversations days apart. The company wants managed components and minimal model token cost per turn. Which components should a solutions architect add? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Per-session state saved in the AgentCore Runtime microVM file system, which is kept between sessions for the same traveller
A step that appends every past conversation of the traveller in full to the system prompt at the start of each new session
An Amazon Bedrock knowledge base over the S3 documents, called by the agent as a retrieval tool for policy and fare questions
A nightly fine-tuning job that trains a custom model on the policy documents so that the agent can answer without retrieval
AgentCore Memory with a long-term memory strategy that extracts user preferences from conversations and retrieves them for new sessions

stem: A financial analytics company is adding an agent that writes and runs Python code to analyse CSV files uploaded by customers. Because the model generates the code, security treats it as untrusted: it must run isolated from the agent's own process and credentials, with no access to the corporate network, and the team does not want to build or patch a sandbox platform. Which approach best meets these requirements?

choices.text: Send the code to a Lambda function that runs it with a role allowed only to read the uploads bucket, attached to a private subnet with routes to on-premises
Use the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter tool in an isolated sandbox without network access, and pass the CSV files into the session
Launch a fleet of hardened EC2 instances in an isolated VPC, run each code snippet in a short-lived Docker container, and copy results back through S3
Run the generated code with exec in the agent's own AgentCore Runtime session, since each session already has a dedicated microVM for one user

stem: A company exposes a scikit-learn fraud-scoring model that runs on CPU and takes about 200 ms per request. Traffic is unpredictable: the API may receive no requests for hours, then a few hundred per minute during campaigns. Callers wait for a synchronous response, and a few seconds of extra latency on the first request after an idle period is acceptable. The company wants to minimise cost and avoid instance management. Which SageMaker AI inference option fits best?

choices.text: An asynchronous inference endpoint that scales to zero instances when idle and writes each result to S3 for the caller to fetch later
A batch transform job started by an EventBridge rule every five minutes that scores all requests collected in S3 since the last run
A real-time endpoint on one small instance with target tracking auto scaling between one and four instances based on invocations per instance
A serverless inference endpoint sized with enough memory for the model and a maximum concurrency that covers campaign peaks

stem: A medical imaging startup runs a GPU segmentation model on 3D scans of 300 to 800 MB each. Processing one scan takes 8 to 20 minutes. Hospitals upload scans in bursts of several hundred, with long quiet periods in between. The startup wants hospitals to submit scans through an API, receive a notification when results are ready, and pay nothing for GPU instances when there is no work. Which SageMaker AI architecture meets these requirements?

choices.text: A real-time endpoint on GPU instances with target tracking auto scaling, with clients that keep the connection open until the segmentation result is returned
A multi-model endpoint on GPU instances that loads the segmentation model from S3 on first use and unloads it after a period with no invocations
A serverless inference endpoint with the maximum memory size and provisioned concurrency, so that burst uploads start without cold starts and stop when quiet
An asynchronous inference endpoint with input and output in S3, Amazon SNS success and error topics, and auto scaling on queue backlog with a minimum of zero instances

stem: A B2B software company trains a separate XGBoost demand model for each of its 3,000 customers. All models use the same container and framework version, each model artifact is under 50 MB, and most customers call their model only a few times per hour. The company currently runs 3,000 real-time endpoints and wants to cut hosting cost sharply and shrink the number of endpoints its operations team deploys and monitors, while keeping real-time responses. Occasional extra latency on a customer's first call after a quiet period is acceptable. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Score every customer each hour with one SageMaker AI batch transform job and serve results from a DynamoDB table keyed by customer ID
Host all models on a small number of multi-model endpoints that load each customer's artifact from S3 on demand and cache it on the instance
Convert each customer's endpoint to a serverless inference endpoint so each one scales to zero independently when that customer has no traffic
Move to multi-container endpoints, putting up to the maximum number of customer containers on each endpoint and invoking the target container directly per request

stem: A company serves a credit-risk model on a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint that handles 2,000 requests per second. Data scientists have a new model version. Before any customer receives its predictions, they want to compare its latency and error rate on real production traffic. After that, the rollout must expose only a small share of traffic first and roll back automatically if CloudWatch alarms fire. Which actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Update the endpoint in place with a new endpoint configuration using all-at-once traffic shifting, and monitor CloudWatch dashboards manually after the switch
Replay last week's requests from S3 through a batch transform job on the new version and compare the scores offline before replacing the model artifact
Use a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting, a baking period, and CloudWatch alarms configured as auto-rollback triggers in the deployment configuration
Add the new version as a second model on a multi-model endpoint and let clients choose it by setting the TargetModel parameter for some requests
Run a SageMaker AI shadow test that sends a copy of live requests to the new version as a shadow variant while only production responses go back to callers

stem: A company hosts six fine-tuned open-weight LLMs on SageMaker AI. Each model needs one GPU, and each currently runs on its own real-time endpoint backed by a 4-GPU instance, so GPU utilisation is under 20%. Traffic per model varies through the day, and two models are idle most nights. The company wants to cut GPU cost while keeping real-time responses, giving each model a guaranteed amount of accelerator and memory, and scaling each model independently. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Deploy the models as inference components on a shared endpoint, set each component's GPU and memory needs, and auto scale each one's copy count, down to zero
Move each model to its own serverless inference endpoint with high memory so that each model scales independently and drops to zero instances overnight
Switch every model to an asynchronous inference endpoint on a smaller GPU instance and scale each endpoint to zero when its request queue is empty
Combine the models into one multi-model endpoint that loads each LLM from S3 when invoked and evicts idle LLMs from GPU memory when another model needs space

stem: A SaaS provider offers a document Q&A feature to 800 business customers using one Amazon Bedrock knowledge base backed by one vector index, to keep cost low. Each customer's documents are in S3 under a prefix named after the tenant ID. Security requires that a query from one tenant can never retrieve chunks from another tenant's documents, even if a user crafts a malicious prompt. Users sign in with Amazon Cognito, whose tokens carry a verified tenant_id claim. Which design meets these requirements?
