choices.text: Write a metadata file with a tenant_id attribute for each document, and have the backend add a tenant_id equals filter to every Retrieve call using the claim from the verified token
Create an Amazon Bedrock guardrail with a denied topic for each tenant's name and apply it to every request, so that content belonging to other tenants is blocked
Add a system prompt telling the model to answer only from documents that belong to the tenant named in the user's question, and reject answers that mention other tenant names
Ask users to include their tenant ID in each question so semantic search ranks their own tenant's chunks highest, and limit retrieval to the top three results

stem: An engineering firm built an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base over 5,000 long equipment manuals using fixed-size chunks of 200 tokens. Evaluations show that retrieval usually finds the right passage, but generated answers often miss the surrounding steps, warnings and table headers that appear in the same section, so answers are incomplete. The firm wants to fix answer completeness without losing retrieval precision. Which change should the solutions architect make?

choices.text: Keep the chunking and switch to an embedding model with more dimensions, then raise the model's temperature so it fills in the missing steps more freely
Switch the data source to hierarchical chunking so small child chunks are matched during search and their larger parent chunks are returned as context
Turn off chunking so that each manual is embedded as a single chunk, then raise the number of retrieved results so that whole manuals are passed to the model
Switch the data source to fixed-size chunks of 2,000 tokens with no overlap so that each chunk always contains a full section of the manual for the model to read

stem: A research publisher is building a Bedrock knowledge base over 150 million paragraph embeddings drawn from its archive. Editors query it a few hundred times per day, mostly during office hours, and sub-second query latency is acceptable. Keyword hybrid search is not needed. The publisher wants the lowest storage and query cost for the vector store and no clusters or capacity to manage. Which vector store should the solutions architect choose?

choices.text: An Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector search collection, because it scales OpenSearch compute units automatically with the indexing and query load
An Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL provisioned cluster with pgvector and HNSW indexes, sized with read replicas to cover the office-hours query load
An Amazon Neptune Analytics graph with vector search, because GraphRAG adds entity relationships between paragraphs to improve retrieval quality
An Amazon S3 Vectors vector bucket and index, because it stores and queries vectors at low cost with sub-second latency and no capacity planning

stem: A manufacturer's support assistant uses an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base on an OpenSearch Serverless vector index with semantic search only. Users often ask about exact part numbers and error codes such as XK-4471 or E-0219. Retrieval returns chunks about similar-looking parts instead, and when the right chunk is found it is often ranked below less relevant ones. Which changes will improve retrieval quality the most? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Increase fixed-size chunks to 3,000 tokens so that more part numbers appear in each chunk and are more likely to be included in results
Change the knowledge base to a larger embedding model by editing its configuration, keeping the existing vectors so that no re-ingestion is needed
Set the knowledge base query to use hybrid search so that keyword matching on exact part numbers and codes is combined with semantic similarity
Raise the generation model's temperature so that it considers a wider range of retrieved chunks when composing the final answer for the user
Add a reranking model to the retrieval configuration so the retrieved candidates are reordered by relevance to the query before generation

stem: An energy company wants a Bedrock knowledge base over 20,000 engineering PDFs in S3. Many PDFs are scans, and key facts sit in tables, charts and diagrams that the default text extraction loses. New and revised PDFs arrive daily, and answers must reflect them by the next morning without reprocessing the unchanged documents. Which ingestion design meets these requirements with the least custom code?

choices.text: Run an Amazon Textract and Lambda pipeline that converts each PDF to plain text in a second bucket, and point the knowledge base data source at that bucket
Keep the default parser, raise chunk overlap to 50 percent so table rows stay together, and run a full re-creation of the knowledge base from scratch every night
Configure the data source with Bedrock Data Automation or a foundation model as parser, and run a scheduled nightly ingestion job that syncs only changed files
Convert each PDF page to an image and store the images in S3, then use a multimodal embedding model so the knowledge base embeds whole pages without parsing

stem: A retailer must regenerate marketing descriptions for about two million catalog items every night with an Amazon Bedrock model. Results only need to be in the product database by the next evening, nobody waits on an individual item, and traffic outside this job is a few thousand interactive requests per day. Finance wants the lowest inference cost without buying capacity that sits idle during the day. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Write the prompts as JSONL records to Amazon S3 each evening and submit Bedrock batch inference jobs, then load the generated descriptions from the output prefix in S3
Purchase a six-month Provisioned Throughput commitment sized for the nightly peak, and route the interactive daytime requests to the same provisioned model to keep it busy
Send the two million prompts on demand with the Priority service tier from an AWS Step Functions Map state so that the whole catalog is processed as early in the night as possible
Host an open-weight model on a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint with GPU instances and target tracking scaling, and send each catalog item as a separate synchronous request

stem: An insurer's claims assistant calls an Amazon Bedrock model through the Converse API. Every request sends the same 30,000-token policy handbook and a fixed set of instructions, followed by a short question from the adjuster. Token costs and time to first response are both higher than planned, and the handbook changes only once a quarter. What should the solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Move the adjuster's question to the start of each prompt and append the handbook after it, so that the model reads the most relevant text first and stops processing the handbook earlier
Put the handbook and instructions first in each prompt with a cache checkpoint after them, so Bedrock prompt caching reuses that prefix and only the short question is processed fresh
Raise the `maxTokens` inference parameter and lower the temperature, so that each answer is complete in one pass and the adjusters do not need to send follow-up questions
Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the model, because requests on provisioned model units are not billed per input token and so the repeated handbook would no longer add any cost

stem: A media company uses one Amazon Bedrock model for two workloads. A customer-facing chat must keep its current response times. A back-office agent enriches archive articles in many steps, each step needs the previous result within a few minutes, and editors accept slower processing if it is cheaper. Both workloads use on-demand Standard today. Which change lowers cost while meeting both requirements?

choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the chat workload and move the enrichment agent onto the same model units at night, so that both use capacity that is already paid for
Move the enrichment agent to Bedrock batch inference jobs so that each step is written to Amazon S3 as one JSONL record and returned at the lower batch inference price
Send both workloads with the Priority service tier, because faster processing finishes each agent step sooner and so reduces the number of tokens that are billed for the archive
Send the enrichment agent's requests with the Flex service tier and keep the customer chat on the Standard tier, choosing the tier per request in each application's model call

stem: An internal help desk assistant on Amazon Bedrock uses the largest model of one model family for every prompt. An analysis of a month of logs shows that most prompts are simple how-to questions that a smaller model of the same family answers equally well, while a minority need complex reasoning. The team wants lower cost without hand-writing classification rules. What should the solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Keep the largest model and send every request with the Priority service tier, so that responses arrive faster and each conversation needs fewer turns to reach an acceptable answer
Send the help desk prompts to a Bedrock batch inference job every few minutes, so that each prompt is billed at the batch price no matter which model ends up answering the question
Use Amazon Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing with a router over the small and large models of that family, and invoke the router ARN in place of the single model ID
Buy Provisioned Throughput for the smaller model and send every prompt to it, accepting that complex questions get weaker answers in exchange for a fixed and predictable monthly bill

stem: A company serves a fine-tuned transformer model from a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint on GPU instances. Traffic is steady around the clock, will stay at this level for at least three years, and the response time must remain within the current SLO. The model architecture is supported by the AWS Neuron SDK. Which TWO actions reduce inference cost? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Purchase a SageMaker AI Savings Plan for the steady hourly instance usage, which applies to real-time inference instances across instance families and Regions
Switch the endpoint to Spot capacity with managed checkpointing, as SageMaker AI training jobs do, and keep one On-Demand instance for fallback
Move the model to SageMaker Serverless Inference with the largest memory setting, so that the GPU instances are no longer billed when they are idle
Buy EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the GPU instance family, because SageMaker AI endpoint instances are billed as regular Amazon EC2 usage in the same account
Compile the model with the Neuron SDK and benchmark it on Inferentia2 (`ml.inf2`) instances, moving the endpoint if latency stays within the SLO

stem: A bank in Frankfurt runs a document assistant on an Amazon Bedrock model in eu-central-1. Regulators require that customer prompts and responses are processed only in EU Regions. Peak traffic now hits the on-demand throughput limit for the model. The bank wants more burst capacity without paying for idle reserved capacity. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Buy Provisioned Throughput in eu-central-1 and in two other EU Regions, and add client-side logic that sends each request to the Region with the most unused model units
Invoke the model through the global cross-Region inference profile, because prompts and responses stay encrypted in transit and logs remain in the eu-central-1 source Region
Move the assistant's model calls to us-east-1, where more on-demand capacity is usually available, and keep the documents and logs stored in the eu-central-1 Region
Invoke the model through the EU geographic cross-Region inference profile from eu-central-1, so requests can be served in other EU Regions during peaks

stem: A FinOps lead reviews a proposal to move a high-volume Amazon Bedrock workload in us-east-1 from direct model calls to a US geographic cross-Region inference profile. She asks how this change affects the bill and where data is kept. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Model invocation logging must be enabled in every destination Region listed in the profile, otherwise requests that are served in those Regions are not recorded in any log
Tokens are billed at the price of the source Region that received the request, and Bedrock adds no separate routing or inter-Region data transfer charge for cross-Region inference
The account must create VPC peering or Transit Gateway peering between the Regions in the profile so that rerouted requests travel privately between AWS Regions
Each request that Bedrock serves from another Region adds an inter-Region data transfer charge per GB on top of the token price, billed to the account that sent the request
Data at rest that the workload configures, such as model invocation logs, stays in us-east-1 as the source Region even when the request is served in another US Region

stem: An organization uses an SCP that denies all actions outside us-east-1 and us-west-2 by using the `aws:RequestedRegion` condition key. A team in us-east-1 switches its application from a foundation model ID to a US geographic cross-Region inference profile whose destination Regions include us-east-2. Calls through the profile now fail with access denied errors, while direct model calls still work. What should the solutions architect do?

choices.text: Change the SCP to allow the Bedrock invoke actions in every Region of the profile, and grant IAM access to the profile and the model in each of those Regions
Create a Bedrock interface VPC endpoint in us-east-2 and route the application's traffic through it, so that requests served in that Region arrive from an allowed private network path
Enable model invocation logging in us-east-2 and attach a resource-based policy to the profile, because Bedrock rejects rerouted requests that cannot be logged in their destination
Replace the profile with a global cross-Region inference profile, because global profiles are evaluated only against the caller's Region and so are not affected by Region-based SCPs

stem: A logistics company calls a US geographic cross-Region inference profile from private subnets in us-east-1. Each request carries scanned delivery documents, and the monthly NAT gateway data processing charge for Bedrock traffic is now larger than the token bill. Security also wants Bedrock calls kept off the internet path. Which change addresses both concerns with the least effort?

choices.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon Bedrock in us-east-1 and add it to the private route tables, because gateway endpoints carry Bedrock traffic without any hourly or data charge
Create interface VPC endpoints for the Bedrock runtime in us-east-1 and in each destination Region of the profile, and join the Regions with Transit Gateway peering for the rerouted traffic
Move the application to public subnets with an internet gateway, so the documents reach the public Bedrock endpoint directly and the NAT gateway data processing charges stop
Create an interface VPC endpoint for the Bedrock runtime in us-east-1 with private DNS enabled, and keep calling the profile there; Bedrock reroutes requests internally

stem: Six business units share one AWS account that runs several applications on the same Amazon Bedrock model with on-demand pricing. Finance needs monthly Bedrock cost per business unit in Cost Explorer for chargeback, and each unit wants to see its own input and output token usage during the month. Which solution meets these requirements with the least operational effort?

choices.text: Estimate each unit's share from the `Duration` metric of each application's Lambda functions, and publish the estimate as a monthly showback report
Create an application inference profile per business unit with a business-unit tag, activate it as a cost allocation tag, and use invocation logs to report token counts
Tag the foundation model's ARN with a business-unit tag for each unit and activate the tag as a cost allocation tag, so that every model invocation is billed under the caller's unit
Create a cost category that splits the monthly Bedrock charge across the six units by their share of Bedrock API calls, as counted in AWS CloudTrail management events

stem: A legal-tech company must choose one of three Amazon Bedrock models for contract summaries. It has 800 real contracts with summaries written by its lawyers. Leadership wants scores for correctness, completeness and faithfulness to the source for every candidate within a week, but only two lawyers are available for review. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Have the two lawyers grade every response of each model in a human-based model evaluation job, using a Likert scale for correctness, completeness and faithfulness
Run a programmatic automatic model evaluation job on each model with a built-in dataset and its accuracy and toxicity metrics, then pick the model with the best mean score
Run an LLM-as-a-judge model evaluation job for each candidate on the 800-contract prompt dataset with reference summaries, scoring correctness, completeness and faithfulness
Deploy all three models behind a weighted router in production for a week and compare the average `InvocationLatency` and `OutputTokenCount` of each model in CloudWatch

stem: A Bedrock knowledge base powers an employee benefits assistant. User reports show answers that are confidently wrong, and the team argues whether retrieval returns the wrong passages or the model ignores correct ones. The team has 300 questions with expected answers. Which TWO actions isolate the cause? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Run a retrieve-only RAG evaluation job on the knowledge base and review the context relevance and context coverage scores against the expected answers
Double the chunk size and the number of retrieved results in the knowledge base, then compare the user complaint rate in the following month with this month's rate
Enable SageMaker AI Model Monitor data quality monitoring on the knowledge base so that drift in the retrieved passages is reported as constraint violations
Run a programmatic model evaluation job on the foundation model alone with a built-in question answering dataset and compare its accuracy to the published baseline
Run a retrieve-and-generate RAG evaluation job and review faithfulness and correctness, to see whether answers stay grounded in the passages returned

stem: A company releases prompt-template and model changes for a Bedrock-based support assistant through AWS CodePipeline. Last month a new template went live and reduced answer correctness, which was found only after customer complaints. The company wants the pipeline to stop any release whose quality scores fall below the current production baseline. What should the solutions architect add?

choices.text: A post-deployment CloudWatch alarm on `InvocationClientErrors` and `InvocationLatency` that rolls the release back when either metric breaches its threshold for an hour
A stage that runs a Bedrock evaluation job on a fixed golden dataset, reads the scores from the job output in S3, and fails the stage if a score is below the baseline
An Amazon Bedrock guardrail with denied topics and content filters on the new version, failing the stage if the guardrail blocks any test prompt during deployment
A manual approval stage where a product owner chats with the new version in staging for ten minutes and approves the release if the answers look reasonable

stem: A hospital group plans to use an Amazon Bedrock model to draft patient discharge instructions. Its clinical governance board requires that licensed nurses on staff judge clinical appropriateness and tone of two candidate models before launch, and patient data must not be shown to anyone outside the organization. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Run a programmatic model evaluation job with the toxicity and robustness metrics, and treat the absence of toxic responses as proof of clinical appropriateness and tone
Run an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation job with a custom metric for clinical appropriateness, and have the judge model's scores signed off by the board in place of any nurse review
Send the drafts to a public crowd workforce through Amazon Augmented AI, so that many independent raters score clinical appropriateness quickly and at a low cost per item
Run a human-based model evaluation job in Bedrock that compares the two models, with a private work team of the hospital's own nurses and rating methods such as Likert scales

stem: A company runs its own fine-tuned model on a SageMaker AI endpoint and is considering a move to an Amazon Bedrock model. The architecture board wants both candidates scored on the same 1,000 prompts with the same judge model and metrics, without moving the self-hosted model into Bedrock first. Which approach meets these requirements with the least effort?

choices.text: Turn on SageMaker AI Model Monitor model quality monitoring on the endpoint and compare its accuracy metrics with the `InvocationLatency` metric of the Bedrock model in CloudWatch
Run SageMaker Clarify on the self-hosted model and a programmatic Bedrock evaluation job on the other, then compare the bias report with the accuracy score in a spreadsheet
Generate the self-hosted model's answers to the prompts, add them to the prompt dataset as its responses, and run Bedrock LLM-as-a-judge jobs for both with the same judge and metrics
Import the self-hosted model into Bedrock with Custom Model Import, wait for the import to finish, and then run the same LLM-as-a-judge evaluation job against both models in Bedrock

stem: A trading-support chatbot calls three different Amazon Bedrock models depending on the request type. The SLO says that 90 percent of calls to each model must complete within 4 seconds, and the on-call team wants to be paged when any one model breaks it. A dashboard on the average of `InvocationLatency` looks healthy while users complain. What should the solutions architect configure?

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail logging of the model invocation API calls, with an EventBridge rule that pages the team whenever a single invocation event shows a response time of over 4 seconds
One CloudWatch alarm on the average of `InvocationLatency` across all models, with the threshold lowered to 2 seconds so that it fires before most users notice the delay
CloudWatch alarms on the p90 statistic of `InvocationLatency` for each `ModelId` dimension, with a 4-second threshold and an SNS topic that pages the on-call team
An alarm on the `Invocations` metric of each model, because rising request counts are the main reason for slow responses and fire before the latency degrades for users

stem: A payments company serves a fraud model from a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint with data capture enabled. Confirmed fraud labels arrive about 30 days after each transaction. The risk team wants an early warning when incoming transaction features shift away from the training data, and later a measured accuracy figure when labels exist. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Run SageMaker Clarify bias analysis once on the training data before deployment, because a balanced training set prevents feature drift from occurring in production
Enable Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging for the endpoint and run a Logs Insights query each week that compares the latest inputs with the training dataset
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the endpoint's `ModelLatency` metric, because feature drift makes the model run more slowly and so latency rises before accuracy falls
Create a data quality monitoring schedule from a baseline of the training data, so captured requests are compared with its statistics and violations reach CloudWatch
Create a model quality monitoring schedule that merges the captured predictions with the ground-truth labels uploaded to Amazon S3 once the fraud outcomes are confirmed

stem: A platform team hosts twelve AI agents built with different open-source frameworks on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. Leadership wants one place to compare agents by session latency, token usage and tool-call error rate, and to drill into a slow session to see which model or tool call took the time. Which approach meets these requirements with the least custom code?

choices.text: Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search, instrument each agent with AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry, and use AgentCore Observability in CloudWatch to compare agents and inspect traces
Log the AgentCore API calls with AWS CloudTrail in each account and build an Amazon Athena view that reconstructs every agent session from the API calls made by the agents
Ask each agent team to write latency and token figures to a shared DynamoDB table at the end of each session, and build a BI dashboard on a nightly export of that table
Attach SageMaker AI Model Monitor schedules to the agents' runtime endpoints, so that latency, token and tool errors are reported as monitoring violations per agent

stem: A company enabled Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging in us-east-1 for its US applications. A new application in eu-central-1 calls the EU geographic cross-Region inference profile. Auditors find no log records for the new application, although its requests succeed and some are served in other EU Regions. What should the solutions architect do?

choices.text: Turn on AWS CloudTrail data events for Bedrock in eu-central-1, because invocation logging does not record requests that are made through cross-Region inference profiles
Enable model invocation logging in eu-central-1 with an S3 bucket or log group destination there, because logging is a per-Region setting and records stay in the source Region
Add the EU profile's ARN to the us-east-1 logging configuration, so that requests from every Region that use this inference profile are written to the existing US log group
Enable model invocation logging in every EU Region listed in the profile, because each record is written in the Region that actually served the request and not where it started

stem: An image-tagging model runs on a SageMaker AI Serverless Inference endpoint. Requests arrive in bursts with quiet periods of 20-40 minutes between them. The p99 end-to-end latency is often several seconds above the SLO for the first requests after a quiet period, while the endpoint's `ModelLatency` stays steady and `ModelSetupTime` shows values at those moments. What should the solutions architect do?

choices.text: Configure Provisioned Concurrency for the serverless endpoint, sized for the first burst, so that initialized capacity is ready when requests resume after a quiet period
Lower the maximum concurrency setting of the endpoint, so that fewer containers are started at once and each request is sent to a container that is already warm
Increase the endpoint's memory size to the maximum value, because the setup time is the model running slowly on too little memory and more memory lowers `ModelLatency` for every request
Enable data capture and a Model Monitor data quality schedule, because the delays come from unusual input images that the model takes longer to set up for processing

stem: A national bank is moving its core analytics platform to Amazon S3, Amazon EBS and Amazon RDS. The banking regulator requires that the root key material protecting customer data is never stored in, or recoverable from, the cloud provider's infrastructure, and that the bank can cut off the cloud services' ability to decrypt the data by acting only on infrastructure it controls. The bank also wants to keep native SSE-KMS integration with these services and avoid changing application code. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create AWS KMS keys with imported key material generated in the bank's on-premises HSM, and delete the imported key material from KMS if access must be cut off
Create AWS KMS keys in an external key store that uses an XKS proxy in front of the bank's on-premises HSMs, and disconnect the proxy if access must be cut off
Create AWS KMS keys in a custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster in the bank's VPC, and delete the CloudHSM cluster if access must be cut off
Encrypt all data on the client side with keys from the bank's on-premises HSMs before upload, and revoke the HSM credentials if access must be cut off

stem: A healthcare provider in a country with no AWS Region runs its patient platform on an AWS Outposts rack in an in-country data center: EC2 instances with EBS volumes, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL on Outposts, and S3 on Outposts for documents. A sovereignty audit finds copies of patient data in the parent Region in a neighboring country. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager takes daily EBS snapshots, and RDS automated backups use default settings. Which change keeps every copy of patient data inside the country?

choices.text: Run a nightly Lambda function that copies each new snapshot and backup from the parent Region to S3 on Outposts and then deletes the copies held in the Region
Encrypt the EBS snapshots and RDS backups with a customer managed KMS key that only in-country administrators may use, and keep the current snapshot and backup locations
Set the Data Lifecycle Manager policies to create EBS local snapshots on the Outpost, and set the RDS backup target to the Outpost for the database instance's backups
Attach an SCP to the platform accounts that denies all actions in the parent Region, so that no snapshot or backup can be written there after the policy takes effect

stem: A payments company processes national identity numbers on Amazon EC2. A regulator requires that plaintext identity numbers be accessible only to a specific, audited tokenization program, and not to operating system administrators of the instances, other processes on the host, or the company's cloud engineers with broad IAM permissions. The decryption key is in AWS KMS. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Run the tokenization program on a dedicated host, restrict SSH with Session Manager and IAM conditions, and allow kms:Decrypt only for the instance role of that host
Run the tokenization program on a Nitro-based instance with encrypted EBS volumes and enable KMS key rotation, so administrators cannot read data at rest on the disk
Store the identity numbers in AWS Secrets Manager with a resource policy that allows only the tokenization role, and rotate the secret every hour with a Lambda function
Run the tokenization program in an AWS Nitro Enclave and add a KMS key policy condition that allows kms:Decrypt only when the enclave attestation matches the signed image

stem: A health-tech company with 40 accounts in AWS Organizations is preparing for an external audit and for onboarding a hospital customer. The auditor asks for independent evidence of the controls that AWS operates for the underlying infrastructure, and the hospital requires that a HIPAA Business Associate Addendum covers every current and future account in the organization. Which actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Open an AWS Support case asking AWS to email the SOC 2 report and a countersigned BAA, because AWS Artifact only provides ISO certificates
Download the AWS SOC 2 Type II report and the PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance from AWS Artifact and share them with the auditor under the Artifact terms
Enable the PCI DSS standard in Security Hub CSPM, which generates a signed AWS Attestation of Compliance for each member account
Deploy the HIPAA operational best practices conformance pack in AWS Config, which activates the BAA once all rules report compliant
From the management account, accept the AWS BAA in AWS Artifact as an organization agreement so that it applies to all member accounts automatically

stem: A financial company runs 300 accounts in AWS Organizations across four Regions. Every quarter, auditors select a date and ask for proof of whether any security group allowed inbound SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 on that date, which resource it was, and when it was fixed. Teams currently answer with screenshots, and evidence older than 90 days is often missing. Which solution provides this evidence with the LEAST ongoing manual effort?

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs for every VPC, deliver them to a central S3 bucket, and use Amazon Athena to find accepted connections on port 22 from public IP addresses for each date
Enable Security Hub CSPM with central configuration in all accounts and Regions, and export the current failed control findings to a spreadsheet at the end of each quarter
Use CloudTrail event history in each account to search for AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress calls, and record the results in a central evidence register every quarter
Record security groups and rule compliance with AWS Config in all accounts and Regions, deploy a restricted-SSH organization Config rule, and query the central history files with Athena

stem: A retailer uses Security Hub CSPM with central configuration and a delegated administrator to run the PCI DSS standard in 90 accounts, with findings aggregated to one Region. For its annual assessment, the Qualified Security Assessor asks for control status evidence covering the full 12-month period, stored where application teams cannot alter it. The security team discovers that findings older than about three months are not available. Which solution fixes this for future assessments?

choices.text: Increase the finding retention period in the Security Hub CSPM delegated administrator settings to 13 months, and restrict who can update findings with an SCP
Schedule a monthly AWS Lambda function that takes a CSV export of the Security Hub CSPM summary dashboard and stores it in a versioned S3 bucket inside each member account
Enable Amazon Security Lake with a delegated administrator in the log archive account, collect Security Hub CSPM findings from all accounts, and set 13-month retention
Enable the AWS Config aggregator in the audit account so that Security Hub CSPM findings are copied into Config compliance history, and keep that history for seven years

stem: An insurance company is designing a claims platform that uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Bedrock. Its risk committee wants a repeatable threat modeling practice that starts before code is written, identifies threats at every trust boundary, links each threat to a mitigation and an owner, and stays current as the design evolves. Which approach meets these goals?

choices.text: Model data flows and trust boundaries at design time, apply STRIDE to each element, record threats and mitigations in Threat Composer stored with the code, and revisit on change
Adopt the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard in Security Hub CSPM and accept the platform's design once all of its controls show as passed
Commission an annual third-party penetration test of the production platform and record its findings in the risk register as the platform's threat model
Enable Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Inspector in every account at launch and treat their findings as the threat model, reviewing them each quarter with the committee

stem: A threat model of a bank's production operations flags a high-risk repudiation threat. Thirty operators federate from the corporate SAML identity provider into one shared OpsAdmin role, then chain into roles in 50 workload accounts. CloudTrail shows only role session names, which operators choose freely, so a harmful change cannot be tied to a person. Which mitigation addresses this risk?

choices.text: Have the identity provider set the SAML SourceIdentity attribute to the operator's user name, and require sts:SourceIdentity in the trust policies of the OpsAdmin role and every chained role
Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation on the organization trail and store the digest files in the log archive account, so every recorded role session can be proven authentic
Tag the OpsAdmin role and every workload role with the names of the operators allowed to use it, and add a condition to each trust policy that checks those tags before allowing the session
Require each operator to pass their corporate user name as the role session name, and publish a runbook that tells operators to reuse the same session name when they chain into workload roles

stem: A threat modeling session for a public customer login API, which runs behind Amazon CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer, identifies two high-severity threats: credential stuffing with stolen username and password lists, and application-layer floods that could exhaust the backend. The company needs preventive mitigations at the edge rather than alerts after the fact. Which actions should the solutions architect take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Run Amazon Inspector network reachability scans on the load balancer and automatically close any listener port that a scan reports as reachable
Enable Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring on the backend and configure it to block source IP addresses that produce repeated failed sign-in attempts
Add the AWS WAF account takeover prevention managed rule group to the web ACL on the CloudFront distribution, scoped to the login request path
Enable Amazon Macie on the S3 bucket that stores application logs so that leaked credentials in failed requests are found and the affected accounts are locked
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced with automatic application layer DDoS mitigation, and add AWS WAF rate-based rules for the login path to the web ACL

stem: A bank uses Amazon Bedrock in two Regions for a customer-facing assistant. Regulators require that the bank retain, for seven years and in tamper-resistant storage, the full text of every prompt sent to a model and every response returned, encrypted with a bank-managed key, along with who invoked the model. The bank already has an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail. What additional configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Add CloudTrail data event selectors for Amazon Bedrock to the organization trail so that the request and response payloads of InvokeModel calls are written to the trail
Enable Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging in both Regions to SSE-KMS buckets with a customer managed key, replicated to an S3 Object Lock bucket with seven-year retention
Enable Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with trace enabled on every request, and forward the guardrail traces to Amazon CloudWatch Logs with a seven-year retention policy
Turn on CloudWatch Logs data protection for the assistant's application log group, and configure the application to log the prompts and responses with a seven-year retention

stem: A pharmaceutical company stores clinical trial data in 12 S3 buckets spread across several accounts in AWS Organizations. A regulation requires a record of every read and write of objects in those buckets for 10 years, proof that log files were not modified or deleted, and that no administrator in a workload account can disable or alter the logging. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Enable S3 server access logging on each of the 12 buckets with delivery to a log bucket in the same account, and apply a lifecycle rule that keeps the log objects for 10 years
Create a CloudTrail Lake event data store in each workload account that collects S3 data events with a 10-year retention, and grant auditors read access to query it
Rely on CloudTrail event history in each workload account, and export its contents weekly to a central bucket with S3 Versioning enabled and a 10-year lifecycle rule
Add S3 data events for only the 12 bucket ARNs to the organization trail with advanced event selectors and log file validation, delivered to an Object Lock bucket in the log archive account

stem: A global retailer encrypts customer data in Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB with one multi-Region KMS key whose primary is in us-east-1, with replicas in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2. Each Region stores only its own customers' data. A new EU rule requires that no KMS key outside the EU can decrypt EU customer data, even if the ciphertext is copied elsewhere. US and APAC operations must not be disrupted. Which approach meets the requirement?

choices.text: Add a statement to the key policy of the eu-west-1 replica that allows kms:Decrypt only when aws:RequestedRegion is eu-west-1, and deny cross-Region copies of the EU buckets and tables
Enable automatic rotation on the existing multi-Region key and rotate it on demand now, so that EU data encrypted from today uses new key material that the old replicas do not hold
Create a new multi-Region key with its primary in eu-west-1 and one replica in eu-central-1, re-encrypt EU data with it, and use an SCP to deny kms:ReplicateKey to non-EU Regions
Make eu-west-1 the primary Region of the existing key with UpdatePrimaryRegion, then schedule deletion of the us-east-1 and ap-southeast-2 replicas so only EU copies of the key remain

stem: A SaaS company serves EU and US business customers from one stack. Customer data is in Amazon DynamoDB global tables with replicas in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. A new EU contract requires EU tenants' data to stay in EU Regions, while a US public-sector contract requires US tenants' data to stay in US Regions. Each tenant has one home jurisdiction, and US users must keep low latency. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Deploy separate EU and US cells, each with global tables replicating only inside its own jurisdiction, and route each request to the tenant's home cell with a tenant-to-cell map
Move all customer data into global tables replicated only between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1, and give US users low latency through AWS Global Accelerator edge locations in the US
Keep the current global tables and add Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing, so that users in Europe are sent to the eu-west-1 stack and users in America to the us-east-1 stack
Keep the current global tables and set replication filters on each replica, so that items whose partition key belongs to an EU tenant are written only to the eu-west-1 replica

stem: A company runs workloads for several teams on virtual machines in another cloud provider and in two on-premises data centers. All workloads get X.509 certificates from one corporate issuing CA, and IAM Roles Anywhere uses that CA as its single trust anchor. An audit finds that any workload with a valid certificate can obtain credentials for the payments team's IAM role. Only certificates whose subject OU is Payments may assume that role. What should the solutions architect do?

choices.text: Attach a permissions boundary to the payments role that allows only the payments team's resources, so other workloads cannot do harm when they assume it
Add a condition to the payments role trust policy that requires aws:PrincipalTag/x509Subject/OU to equal Payments, along with the trust anchor ARN as aws:SourceArn
Create a second trust anchor that uses the same issuing CA certificate and a separate profile for the payments role, and tell the payments workloads to use that profile
Attach a session policy to the Roles Anywhere profile that denies all actions unless the request comes from the IP address ranges of the payments workloads

stem: Servers in an on-premises factory use IAM Roles Anywhere with certificates from the company's own CA, which publishes a certificate revocation list. Each server's certificate has a unique subject CN. One server is stolen, and its certificate, valid for another 11 months, has just been revoked at the CA. The stolen server must not obtain new credentials or keep using existing ones, while the 400 other servers that use the same trust anchor and role must keep working. Which actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disable the trust anchor in IAM Roles Anywhere until the stolen certificate expires, and re-enable it after the company issues new certificates to the other servers
Delete the IAM role and create a new role with the same permissions and trust policy, then update the profile so the other servers use the new role
Configure the trust anchor to check the certificate's OCSP responder URL on every request, so the revoked certificate is rejected without importing anything
Import the CA's updated certificate revocation list into IAM Roles Anywhere for the trust anchor, so new sessions with the revoked certificate are rejected
Add an inline policy to the role that denies all actions when aws:PrincipalTag/x509Subject/CN equals the stolen server's CN, so its unexpired credentials stop working

stem: A logistics company exposes a business-to-business API on an internet-facing Application Load Balancer. Each of 300 partners must authenticate with a client certificate issued by the company's AWS Private CA; connections without a valid certificate, or with a revoked one, must be refused before reaching the application, and the application must know which partner is calling. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Keep the ALB HTTPS listener, install an ACM private certificate on it, and allow only partner IP ranges in the load balancer security group to identify which partner is calling
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer TCP listener, and run a fleet of reverse proxies on EC2 that verify client certificates and forward partner identity to the application
Enable mutual TLS in verify mode on the ALB HTTPS listener with a trust store built from the CA bundle and its CRL, and read the partner identity from the client certificate headers the ALB adds
Enable mutual TLS in passthrough mode on the ALB HTTPS listener, and have the application validate each forwarded client certificate chain and CRL before it processes a request

stem: A regulator now requires that a public payments endpoint accept only TLS 1.3. The endpoint is an internet-facing Application Load Balancer with an ACM public certificate, forwarding HTTPS to nginx on Amazon EC2. The team configured nginx to allow only TLS 1.3, but an external scan still shows that TLS 1.2 handshakes succeed against the public hostname. What should the team do?

choices.text: Change the target group protocol from HTTPS to HTTP so the load balancer stops negotiating TLS 1.2 with nginx, and keep the listener policy unchanged
Set the ALB HTTPS listener's security policy to ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-3-2021-06, which accepts only TLS 1.3, and keep the ACM certificate on the listener
Reissue the ACM certificate with an ECDSA P-384 key instead of RSA 2048, because ACM certificates with elliptic curve keys negotiate only TLS 1.3 with clients
Add a security group rule on the ALB that drops TLS 1.2 ClientHello packets, and keep the listener's default security policy for compatibility with monitoring tools

stem: A company runs about 20,000 short-lived pods on Amazon EKS that use mutual TLS between services. Security requires certificates from a company-controlled private CA, a maximum certificate lifetime of 24 hours, and no dependency on CRL or OCSP infrastructure. Certificates are requested automatically by cert-manager through the AWS Private CA issuer plugin. The current general-purpose CA is costly at this issuance volume. Which change best meets the requirements at the LOWEST cost?

choices.text: Request ACM public certificates for each service name, and have cert-manager export them into Kubernetes secrets that the pods load at startup each day
Keep the general-purpose CA, issue 24-hour certificates from it, and configure CRL distribution to an S3 bucket so every service checks revocation status
Keep the general-purpose CA, issue certificates valid for 13 months, and publish an OCSP responder so that compromised pod certificates can be revoked quickly
Create a subordinate CA in AWS Private CA using short-lived certificate mode, and have cert-manager issue 24-hour certificates from it without revocation checking

stem: A financial company is moving a self-managed Oracle Database from its data center to Amazon EC2. It uses Oracle Transparent Data Encryption with the master key in an on-premises HSM accessed through PKCS#11. The regulator requires a single-tenant HSM validated at FIPS 140 Level 3, in which only the company's own crypto officers can create and manage users and keys, and the vendor has no access to key material. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Deploy an AWS CloudHSM cluster with HSMs in two Availability Zones, and configure Oracle TDE on EC2 to use the CloudHSM PKCS#11 library for the master key
Import the master key into AWS KMS as external key material, set it to expire after one year, and configure Oracle TDE to wrap tablespace keys with the KMS key
Use an AWS KMS customer managed key with automatic rotation for the EBS volumes, and turn off Oracle TDE because the KMS HSMs are FIPS validated at Level 3
Create an AWS KMS key in a CloudHSM custom key store, and configure Oracle TDE on the EC2 instances to call the KMS key through the PKCS#11 interface

stem: A payment processor signs transactions with keys in an AWS CloudHSM cluster in eu-west-1 that currently has one HSM. The regulator requires that signing survives the loss of an Availability Zone, that the company can rebuild signing capability in eu-central-1 within four hours if eu-west-1 becomes unavailable, and that keys never exist outside an HSM in plaintext. Which actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Export the signing keys in plaintext with the key management utility to an encrypted S3 bucket with Cross-Region Replication to eu-central-1, and import them later
Copy the cluster's backups to eu-central-1 with the copy backup to Region feature, and create a new cluster from the latest copied backup if eu-west-1 fails
Enable multi-Region replication on the CloudHSM cluster so that every key created in eu-west-1 is automatically and synchronously created in a cluster in eu-central-1
Create AWS KMS multi-Region keys in a CloudHSM custom key store and replicate them to eu-central-1, so the signing keys are available in both Regions
Add a second HSM to the cluster in a different Availability Zone of eu-west-1, so the cluster synchronizes keys and the client spreads requests across both HSMs
